Tāyumānavar
(A. D. 1705-1742)
------------------------------------------
Tāyumānavar was a great Śaiva saint of Tamil Nadu. He is still a living force in the religious life of Tamil country.
He was a veḷḷāḷa by caste and was attached to the great शिव temple at Vedāraṇyam near Tanjavoor (Tanjore). By virtue of his learning and character he became a high official in the court of the Naik ruler, Vijayaraṅga Cokkanāthar, of Tiruchirapalli. Since he yearned for spiritual wisdom he gave up his job and spent his time in sādhana under an able guide.
He composed quite a few poems in Tamil, making an attempt to synthesise Vedānta with शैवसिद्धान्त. He rose above the narrow religious disputes and reached high levels of philosophical wisdom.
